pairs.why: B has the real card's slab top on a plain rectangular block pedestal with a square base plate and straight-sided stools, while A swells the pedestal into a tiered flared column and gives the stools hourglass waists.
B has a short barrel with a thin, rounded U-strap yoke and a slim mount, close to the real fixture, while A uses a long tapering can with a boxy rectangular bracket.
A keeps the real clock's true circle with a thick even rim and a flat face, while B squashes the clock into a tilted ellipse.
A's dome and its thick tube are compact and simple like the real chunky forms, while B adds more small thin parts (tank, legs, ladder), but neither is clearly closer.
B's can is short and compact with a thin rounded strap yoke like the real one, while A has a long can and a thick square-cornered bracket.
B has the real chair's thick rolled seat edge, wrapped top of the back, and X legs, while A has a thin flat seat with a bare bar and spindly wire legs.
A's brim curls up at the sides and has a tall pinched crown, a real cowboy-hat shape, while B's brim is flat and wide with a short crown, so it reads as a sombrero.
B has the full set of parts (rings, nozzle, swept fins, two portholes) and a believable slender body, while A is a fattened toy-like blob with small flat fins.
